name: Autosomal Recessive Syndromic Cerebellar Ataxia
aliases: Autosomal Recessive Cerebellar Ataxia with Syndromic Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Recessive Syndromic Cerebellar Ataxia

criteria.description: Progressive cerebellar ataxia evidenced by gait and limb incoordination
Presence of additional syndromic features such as dysarthria, oculomotor abnormalities, and peripheral neuropathy
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in causative genes associated with autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia
Exclusion of acquired or other hereditary ataxias by clinical, laboratory, and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with syndromic features plus genetic confirmation of biallelic pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive clinical evaluation and genetic testing to confirm autosomal recessive inheritance.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Oculomotor abnormalities including nystagmus and saccadic pursuit
searchTerms: eye movement problems like shaking eyes
difficulty tracking moving objects with eyes
nerve damage affecting sensation and movement
peripheral nerve problems with mixed symptoms

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment ranging from mild to moderate
Skeletal deformities such as pes cavus or scoliosis
searchTerms: foot arch deformities or curved spine
high foot arches or sideways spine curve
skeletal deformities like scoliosis or pes cavus

rare.symptomName: Endocrine abnormalities such as diabetes mellitus

laboratory: Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein in some subtypes
Normal routine blood tests excluding acquired causes
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar atrophy predominantly affecting the vermis and hemispheres
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in genes such as SYNE1, SACS, or other AR cerebellar ataxia-associated genes

distinguishingFeatures: Autosomal recessive inheritance with early onset
GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in FXN gene

redFlags: Rapid progression of ataxia with early loss of ambulation
Presence of cerebellar ataxia with multisystem involvement
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
references: Orphanet: Autosomal Recessive Syndromic Cerebellar Ataxia - ORPHA:98099
Recent review article on hereditary cerebellar ataxias, Neurology Journal, 2024
